g.text: Why the Panama Canal ran short of water
every claim against the line it sits under

svg.text: The topic line shatters into verified source cards: rainfall −41% (Oct 2023),
50,000,000 gallons a crossing, a 26 m lock climb, a map and an archive print. Each
Cards fly out from the line along curved paths, rotate to 0° and snap into a grid.
Checks pop in 80ms after each lands.
Paper flicks; a small "tick" per verified check.
Cards collapse into lines of text.

g.text: In October 2023, the rain didn't come.
Gatun Lake fell to its lowest level in years.
Every ship that crosses uses 50 million gallons of fresh water.
The locks climb 26 metres, one chamber at a time.
So the canal did the only thing it could.

svg.text: Sources collapse into a structured script. Numbered beats; each line tagged with the
visual it needs (MAP, CHART, DIAGRAM). Line 03 is highlighted.
Text lines slide in from the right and lock to a baseline grid. Tags snap on after
their line. Highlight bar wipes across line 03.
Typewriter-soft ticks, much quieter than Act I.
The script lines stretch sideways into a waveform.

g.text: Every ship that crosses uses 50 million gallons…
VO · EN · 00:54 · IN YOUR CHANNEL'S VOICE

svg.text: The script lines stretch horizontally into bars, and the bars become a green voice
waveform spanning the frame. Label VO · EN.
Object transformation (the brief's transition system): each text line scales X ×4 and
loses its letters into bars over 12 frames; bars ripple into waveform peaks.
A breath, then the first syllable of the read, bit-crushed into a soft digital
Waveform drops into a timeline track.
The waveform drops into A1 of an edit timeline. Map, archive and lock-diagram clips
fly into V1; graphics (−41%, 26 m, 50M gal) into V2; music bed into A2. Programme
Clips slide in on their tracks and butt-join with a satisfying snap. Playhead sweeps;
Timeline snaps (magnetic clicks), a quick scrub.
Timeline folds up into a single player.
